deliverables: Instant on-chain distribution of the withdrawal amount to the intended recipient as part of governance action enactment
request.recipient: Ikigai Info governance action submitter; specific recipient address not stated in document
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to reimburse the unrecovered deposit from the Ikigai Info governance action and compensate claimed lost staking rewards.

claims.claim: The proposal says an Info governance action titled "Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai -" was submitted in September 2024 shortly after the Chang hard fork.
The proposal says the Ikigai action was symbolic and asked the community to agree with a statement thanking contributors and expressing hope for Cardano's future.
The proposal says a Cardano node bug allowed an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering a 100000 ADA deposit.
The proposal says community sentiment at the time favored reimbursing the deposit because the submitter should not lose 100000 ADA for being an early governance pioneer.
The proposal says no entity-based budget submissions included this reimbursement after treasury withdrawals became available following the Plomin hard fork.
The proposal says the Cardano in Oceania initiative included the reimbursement in its budget Info governance action, but that action was not approved.
The proposal requests 103000 ADA, consisting of the original 100000 ADA deposit plus 3000 ADA for claimed lost staking rewards at 2% per annum.
The proposal says the requested amount does not exceed the current Net Change Limit.
The proposal says the recipient has not previously received funds from the treasury.
The proposal says no audit or oversight budget is needed because the funds will be distributed directly and auditable on-chain.

summary: The document requests 103000 ADA to reimburse a claimed unrecoverable 100000 ADA governance-action deposit and 3000 ADA of claimed lost staking rewards, but provides limited supporting analysis beyond a reference link and assertions about constitutionality, NCL compliance, and on-chain auditability.
